newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end higher for second day.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end higher for second day.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended slightly higher for the second day in a row Friday, as the complex continued to stabilize following gold's slide to new three-year lows this week on news of a 300 tonne gold sale by the Dutch central bank.

"It was a day for a breather on moderate volumes, ahead of the holiday on Monday," FIMAT New York trader John Tyree said. "Some funds have been short covering this week but the dollar is strong and producers may not be done hedging."
COMEX remains open on Monday, but the Martin Luther King Jr holiday may slow trade, analysts said.
COMEX February gold ended up $1.40 an ounce at $356.40, after trading a $355.00-357.10 range, with total volume estimated at 40,000 lots.
Spot gold in the bullion market ended quoted $355.30/80, compared to the London Friday afternoon fix at $355.75 and the New York close Thursday at $354.10/60.
Some fund shortcovering has been occurring in the past two days though as gold's downward momentum looked to be running out of steam for now as gold neared $350 level, traders said.
Open interest in COMEX February gold fell 3,570 lots Thursday, in data released Friday, while total open interest fell 2,463 lots.

The US dollar surged to new two-and-a-half year high against the mark and Swiss franc, and tested its 46 month high seen earlier this week against yen, while the dollar's trade weighted index saw a new 30 month high also at 90.50, after better-than-expected US November trade data.
"Throughout 1996 import demand in some Asian markets dropped significantly," Smith Barney analyst David Rinehimer said.

"The most recent data indicated year-on-year declines in gold imports of 51 percent for Japan, due in part to a much stronger US dollar against the yen, while Hong Kong gold imports fell 30 percent and Taiwan demand was down 12 pct."

The price of gold in South African rand fell to a three month low this week around 1640 rand, while the price of gold in Australian dollars remained near its four-and-a-half year low at $450 an ounce seen in December.
Australia's Newcrest Mining reported hedging 3.7 million ounces of gold in the forward market out over the next decade last week, while more Australian producer hedging was noted this week.
Rising gold mine production from Australia and Canada this year, is expected to offset a further drop in output from South Africa, the world's largest producer.
Silver remained relatively resilient though, with the spot gold/silver ratio declining further Friday to 74.48 at the close, a new four month low.
COMEX March silver ended 3.2 cents at $4.772 an ounce, after seeing a $4.735-4.810 range.
The April COMEX gold/NYMEX silver ended slightly lower though at $6.60 an ounce.
NYMEX April platinum closed up 70 cents at $365.10, while NYMEX March palladium ended up 50 cents at $126.00.
